answer: Agents can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may influence a market, then randomly audit a small share of its claims against costly evidence. If a cluster of supposedly independent agents reuses evidence or coordinates false reports, audits expose the links and slash their deposits; creating more identities does not multiply influence without more capital at risk. A kernel of trusted reviewers can seed an ember of suspicion and trigger checks across an orchard of accounts, but the attacker must keep funding every exposed identity and may lose the stake.
